contract.settlement_definition: Three series, one winner each, after the 2026-11-09 split (exhibition games and the MVP now sit in unreg:all_star_exhibition_games and unreg:all_star_game_mvp). KXNBA3PTCONTEST and KXNBASLAMDUNK settle Yes if the named player wins the stated year's contest; a player who drops out, withdraws or does not participate resolves No (not void). The 3PT contest has two rounds of 70-second shooting from several 3-point locations; the top three scorers of round one advance and the highest championship-round score decides, so round-one scores do not carry. The dunk contest has four players, two judged dunks each in round one, two finalists by combined score, and the two final-round dunks' higher combined score decides. KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS settles Yes if the named team wins the 2026 Shooting Stars contest 'originally scheduled for February 14, 2026'; its sampled rules_secondary is empty, so the format, ties, team changes and non-participation are not in Kalshi's text. The league's official 2026 rules PDF (read directly, sha256 ed035e65...b921) gives four teams of three, seven locations worth 2/2/2/3/2/3/4 points, a 1:10 clock, top two advancing, a 30-second first-round tiebreaker and a full 1:10 final tiebreaker; it is league material, not Kalshi text, and Kalshi-specific application stays unknown (see u10b). No sampled rule names a source of truth or treats shoot-offs, dunk-offs or tied final rounds.

rules_evidence.quote: The top three scorers from the first round advance to the championship round, where the highest score determines the winner.
rules_evidence.establishes: Two-round format with three finalists; final-round score alone decides (round-1 score does not carry over).

rules_evidence.quote: players attempt to score as many points as possible from multiple 3-point locations within 70 seconds
rules_evidence.establishes: The round is timed (70 s) over several locations, so release tempo and location-specific accuracy matter; ball values are not stated.

rules_evidence.quote: If the player drops out, withdraws, or does not participate in the contest for any reason, the market resolves to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: Withdrawal of the named entrant resolves No rather than void, so field-withdrawal hazard maps directly to the No side.

rules_evidence.quote: In the first round, all four players will attempt two dunks, and the combined score will determine the top two who advance to the final round.
rules_evidence.establishes: Four entrants, two judged dunks in round 1, two finalists; judging scale and dunk-off procedure are not stated.

rules_evidence.quote: Each finalist will then attempt two additional dunks, with the higher combined score determining the champion.
rules_evidence.establishes: Final is decided on the two final-round dunks' combined score only; tie handling is unstated.

rules_evidence.quote: If Team Knicks wins the 2026 Pro Basketball All-Star Shooting Stars contest
rules_evidence.establishes: Shooting Stars entrants are franchise-named teams; no format, scoring or withdrawal clause is given in the rules text.

variants_and_edge_cases: Withdrawal: the 3PT and dunk rules say a non-participating named player resolves No; KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS has no such clause, so a renamed, merged or substituted team is unhandled by the text.
3PT contest: the final-round score decides; round-1 ties for third place and final-round ties (shoot-off) are not described in the rules, and ball values and rack layout are not in Kalshi's text.

Dunk contest: judging scale, number of judges, attempt limits and dunk-off on ties are not in the rules; only round structure is, and the round-one combined score selects the two finalists but does not carry into the final.

KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS: Kalshi's rules_secondary is empty and its text gives only the team name and the originally scheduled date. The league's official 2026 rules PDF says the higher final-round score wins, a tied final is rerun for the full 1:10 and a round-1 tie that decides advancement is rerun at 30 seconds, and that a team is disqualified for missing a valid attempt at a location or for shooting from locations out of order; Kalshi does not say it adopts these, and the PDF does not state the consequence of disqualification, so ties, disqualification, replay and cancellation handling stay unknown for settlement (u10b).
Event postponement: the Shooting Stars rule says 'originally scheduled for' a date, so a rescheduled contest stays live; cancellation of a contest is not addressed in any of the three texts.
Other All-Star Weekend series (the exhibition games and the MVP) were split out on 2026-11-09 and are no longer claimed by this record.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not named in any sampled rule; assumed to be the NBA's official announcement of each contest's winner (NBA.com results/press release). Kalshi's own determination governs if it differs.

mechanism.summary: Three series settle on the winner of a one-off All-Star Saturday skills contest: the individual 3-Point Contest, the judged Slam Dunk Contest and the three-player-team Shooting Stars. The outcome is generated in layers: the league invites a field and withdrawal resolves a named player's market to No; entrants produce performance (timed racks shot with no defender, judged dunks with a miss risk, or a team of two NBA players and a legend shooting from seven fixed locations against a 1:10 clock); the format converts performance to a winner through rounds, advancement cuts, a final that resets scores and tie procedures. Winners are maxima over a few noisy scores, so favourites are capped and format parameters (ball or spot values, rounds, tie rules) matter as much as skill; regular-season counting-stat machinery is mostly irrelevant, and each series uses its own scoped inputs (contract.series_input_scope). The exhibition-game and MVP chains no longer belong here.

stages.name: Contest field formation and withdrawal
stages.description: Contest fields are produced by league invitation and acceptance (3PT and dunk entrants, Shooting Stars teams of two NBA players and a legend), then changed by injury, doubling up with other weekend events and replacement by the league up to the day before. For the 3PT and dunk series a withdrawn named player resolves No, so participation probability multiplies every Yes price; the Shooting Stars rules text has no such clause, so a team change is unhandled and a roster change flows into team skill instead.
stages.distribution: Discrete set membership; withdrawal is a Bernoulli per entrant, correlated when an entrant is also in another weekend event.

stages.name: Contest skill: location-specific rack shooting, tempo and dunk repertoire
stages.description: In the 3PT contest each shooter has 70 seconds (rules) for racks at several locations with no defender; skill is per-location make probability, deep-range accuracy for bonus balls, choice of the all-money-ball rack location and release tempo, since unreleased balls score zero. In the dunk contest the analogue is the repertoire of difficulty tiers and conversion within attempts. Season box scores predict these only through open catch-and-shoot and location splits plus prior contest record.
stages.distribution: Per-ball Bernoulli with positive within-round correlation (beta-binomial); dunk make is Bernoulli by tier with a miss penalty, so scores are a bimodal mixture.

stages.name: Contest format aggregation: rounds, advancement, final reset and shoot-offs
stages.description: Round scores become a winner through the format: in the 3PT contest the top three of round one advance and the final-round score alone decides (rules), so round-one scores do not carry; in the dunk contest the top two of four advance and the two final dunks decide. Ties go to shoot-offs or dunk-offs that the rules do not describe. The maximum over noisy scores means the best shooter wins well under half the time.
stages.distribution: Discrete scores with ties; the winner is an extreme-value statistic over finalists, so upset probability is high and shoot-offs are not rare.

stages.name: Judging of dunks
stages.description: Judges score each dunk on a bounded scale, so a dunk's value is a function of difficulty, execution, creativity and crowd response, and scores compress near the top. The panel's composition (former players, celebrities), the sequence of contestants and the use of props all shift scores, and per the rules round-one combined scores only select the two finalists, after which the two final-round dunks alone decide the champion; dunk-offs on ties are not in the rules.
stages.distribution: Ordinal bounded scores with heavy ceiling mass; ties common; panel effects shared across all contestants.

stages.name: Shooting Stars team contest: spots, clock, two rounds
stages.description: Four teams (Team All-Star, Team Knicks, Team Cameron, Team Harper; only the Knicks name is a franchise) of two NBA players plus a legend shoot one team at a time for 1:10 from seven locations in order 1 to 7 worth 2, 2, 2, 3, 2, 3 and 4 points: each player takes one shot at each of locations 1-6 in the team's declared order and then shoots in that order as many times as the clock allows at location 7 (the 4-point spot), with a left-wing passer and the team advancing as a unit (official NBA 2026 Kia Shooting Stars rules PDF (read directly 2026-11-09, sha256 ed035e65...b921; completeness/source_provenance/NBA_2026_Shooting_Stars.json): four teams of three (two NBA players plus one NBA Legend); seven locations shot in order 1 to 7 worth 2, 2, 2, 3, 2, 3, 4 points (right-lane layup/dunk, 18-ft right baseline, right elbow, right-wing three, top of the key, left-corner three, long-range three); each player takes one shot at each of locations 1-6 in the team's declared shooting order and at location 7 players shoot in that order as many times as the clock allows; a designated passer at the left wing feeds each shot; the team advances as a unit; 1:10 clock per team per round; the top two of four teams advance from round 1; the lower round-1 team shoots first in the final and the higher final-round score wins; a tied round-1 result that decides advancement is rerun among the tied teams only at 30 seconds (round-1 scores ignored); a tied final is rerun for the full 1:10; a shot out of the declared player order does not count (and, other than at location 7, that player does not shoot again); a team is disqualified if not all players make valid attempts from a location or if it shoots from locations out of order). All four shoot in round 1, the top two repeat in a final and the higher final-round score wins; a round-1 tie that decides advancement is rerun at 30 seconds among the tied teams only, a tied final is rerun for the full 1:10. The PDF itself does not define a valid shot attempt, does not say what disqualification does to a team's score or advancement, does not say whether the 30-second tiebreaker still runs locations 1-6 in full, and does not say the two players must be current NBA players. Kalshi's text adds only the team name and the originally scheduled date, so how Kalshi applies the league rules to settlement (ties, disqualification, replay, cancellation, a changed format) is unknown. Team skill mixes the NBA players' spot make rates with an age-discounted legend, and the winner is the higher of two team scores in the final after a selection stage.
stages.distribution: Sum over three players of correlated timed make processes with 2-4 point jumps; discrete team scores (2026 finals near 38-47) with ties possible; a maximum over four teams in round 1 then a head-to-head final.

stages.name: Settlement of the three contest winners
stages.description: Each series settles on the officially announced winner. Rules text confirms withdrawal-to-No for the 3PT and dunk series, the 3PT round and advancement structure and the dunk round structure, and is silent on shoot-offs, dunk-offs, tied final rounds and any Shooting Stars format, tiebreak, disqualification or team-change clause; the sampled Shooting Stars text is only the team name and date. The league's own rules PDF gives the format and tiebreakers, but Kalshi does not say it adopts them, so the winner is whatever the league declares champion and Kalshi's treatment of ties, disqualification, replay and cancellation is unknown.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the official result; ambiguity mass sits in rare branches (ties, shoot-offs, cancellation, renamed teams).

talent_strength.note: Per series: dunk pedigree, 3PT shooting transferred to a defender-free setting, Shooting Stars team skill including the legend.

opponent_matchup.note: The skills contests have no defence and no head-to-head matchup other than the final-round comparison of scores; the matchup content of the team exhibitions moved to unreg:all_star_exhibition_games.

role_personnel.note: Field and team membership; who shoots the high-value last spot in Shooting Stars.

availability_news.note: Injuries and announcements before the weekend.

coaching_scheme.note: The three contests have no coaches or schemes; shooting order and rack or spot placement are the entrant's own choices and sit in the spot-and-tempo profile, not in a coaching input.

environment.note: Neutral site; venue-year sightline/rim offset for the shooting contests.

game_context_script.note: Round structure, advancement cuts, final reset and ties are the only 'script' (no game state).

pace_volume.note: Balls or attempts released inside the 70-second clock.

efficiency_conversion.note: Make rates by location (3-point racks, 2-point Shooting Stars spots) and dunk conversion under contest conditions.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Effort and motivation (prize money, doubling up across Rising Stars, contests and the Game, home-market entrants) have no measurable pregame proxy defined for the three contests.

catalog_entry.label: NBA All-Star Weekend skills contests (3-point, slam dunk, Shooting Stars)
catalog_entry.target: Winner of an All-Star Weekend skills contest: the 3-Point Contest, the Slam Dunk Contest or the Shooting Stars team contest
catalog_entry.mechanism: Each series settles on the winner of a one-off skills contest: the league invites the field and a withdrawn named player resolves No (3PT, dunk); performance is timed rack shooting with no defender, judged dunks with a miss risk, or a three-player team (two current players and a legend) shooting from seven fixed spots against a 70-second clock; the format turns performance into a winner through rounds, advancement cuts, a final that resets scores and tie procedures. Winners are maxima over a few noisy scores, so favourites are capped and format parameters matter as much as skill. Inputs are scoped per series because the three processes are disjoint.

inputs.why: Format parameters decide scoring scale, ties and the number of rounds, so they define what a win means in each series.
Simulated winner distribution over rounds, advancement and shoot-offs is the direct model of the 3-point contest.
Contest make rate is a catch-and-shoot skill without a defender; this input converts game stats to that setting.
The dunk series settles on panel scores, so judge behaviour and ties are the mechanism.
Dunk tier choice and make rate under attempt caps drive expected judged score.
Only pregame talent measure for contestants who rarely appear in season statistics.
Contest fields change before the event, shifting every entrant's winning probability.
Injury reports before the weekend drive withdrawals and replacement players across all three events.
Announcements on field, captains, format and participation arrive as news before official lists.
Open-shot make probability by shot type is the best game-data proxy for rack shooting.
Hot-hand dispersion of makes inside a minute-long round sets contest score variance.
Free-throw skill is a low-noise proxy for shooting form in a defender-free setting.
Arena sightlines, backdrop and rim feel shift contest conversion for all entrants.
Format changes announced by the league alter scoring rules for the Game and contests.
Announcement timing of rosters, fields and format sets the as-of date for every input.
Rules fix withdrawal-to-No, the 70 s round, dunk rounds, the 12-minute round robin and 40/25 targets; two series have primary text only.
Official winner announcements are the labels and need reconciling with the contract source.
Location splits, deep-ball rate, rack placement and release tempo convert a shooter to the 70-second contest's scoring.
Shooting Stars is a team shooting contest; this input carries team skill and the explicit UNVERIFIED format parameters (spot values, tie rules) instead of silently assuming them.

Four of seven reported Shooting Stars spots are 2-point spots that the 3-point-only spot profile cannot estimate, so team skill needs rim, baseline, elbow and top-of-key conversion and tempo for current players and legends.

interactions.hypothesis: Win probability is a max-of-noisy-scores function of per-ball make rates, so a shooter's gain from a few points of make probability is bigger when the field is thin at the top and shrinks as more strong shooters enter.

Judged score saturates near the scale maximum, so extra difficulty adds little once a clean dunk already earns near-perfect marks, while a miss subtracts a lot; this reverses the naive hard-dunk advantage.
A withdrawal changes the winner probability differently depending on the number of finalists and rounds: with fewer rounds a replacement has a larger chance to win through variance.

The gain from placing the all-money rack at a shooter's best location depends on the ball values and whether deep bonus balls exist in that year's format; a large location split is worth more when money balls carry double value and less when deep balls dominate the maximum.

If the reported spot values hold (2, 2, 2, 3, 2, 3, 4), a make at the long-range last spot is worth twice a layup, so a team's expected score depends on which of its three players shoots that spot and how many attempts it gets inside 70 seconds; a legend with a poor long-range rate is cheap at the layup spot and costly at the last one, so team skill is a lineup-and-spot assignment, not a team average.

The Shooting Stars winner needs a top-two round-1 score and then a higher final score, so the favourite's advantage is compounded over two noisy draws and the second round can be won by a team that was only second in round one; ties for the second final slot or in the final switch the outcome to a shoot-off or replay procedure that the rules text does not state, so tie mass is its own regime.

nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.label: All-Star Weekend format and rules ledger by event and year
nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.mechanism: Each event's winner is a deterministic function of the format: racks, balls, money-ball value, time limit, number of rounds, how many advance, tiebreak or shoot-off, dunk attempt caps and judging scale, All-Star Game length, target score and team structure.
nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.rationale: The formats are changed almost every few years (the Game has switched between East-West, captains' draft and a multi-team mini-tournament), so a historical result is only a label for the same process if the format parameters are matched. The subtle part is that a rule change moves variance and ties, not just level: a shorter game or a single-elimination final increases upset probability.
nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.measurement: Per event-year and per series (3PT, dunk, ASG, Rising Stars, Shooting Stars, MVP): participants, rounds, advancement count, balls per rack, racks, points per ball type (regular, money ball, deep-zone ball), seconds per round, shoot-off rule, dunks per round and attempt limit, judge count and score range, ASG game length or target score, number of teams, team-assignment rule (conference, draft, nationality), round-robin tiebreak order, Rising Stars semifinal/final targets, Shooting Stars team size and scoring, MVP selection method. Each field carries a provenance flag: RULES_TEXT (quoted Kalshi rule, e.g. 70 s, 40/25 targets, 1-1-1 point-differential tiebreak), LEAGUE_RELEASE, or SOURCE_UNVERIFIED; as-of = the league announcement date. Every historical label joins to its own format vector.
free_sources: NBA.com and NBA Communications press releases
nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.why: Format parameters set the tie, upset and score-scale behaviour of all three Kalshi series; without them past winners cannot be pooled.

sources.name: NBA 2026 Kia Shooting Stars official rules (PDF): format, 7 locations and 2/3/4 point values, 1:10 clock, tiebreakers, violations
sources.note: primary source for the 2026 event; verbatim extract and rendered-table reading in completeness/source_provenance/; says nothing about how Kalshi settles ties, disqualification, replay or cancellation

sources.name: Basketball-Reference

nba.threept_contest_score_pmf.label: Three-Point Contest round-score distribution and winner simulation
nba.threept_contest_score_pmf.mechanism: Each shooter's round score is a sum over racks of correlated Bernoulli makes with different point weights; the winner is the maximum over finalists after advancement, with ties broken by a shoot-off.
nba.threept_contest_score_pmf.rationale: The winner is a max-of-noisy-scores over a field of about eight, so the favourite's chance is capped well below his skill edge; the round-score SD is several points, comparable to the skill gap between the best and median shooter (per-ball make probability is a parameter to be estimated, not a fact). Only the final-round score decides (rules), so round-1 advancement variance and final-round tie mass both matter.
nba.threept_contest_score_pmf.measurement: For each entrant simulate ball by ball: P(make) per location from nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile (regular, money-ball and deep-zone balls), the shooter's chosen all-money-ball rack location, balls actually released within 70 s from the tempo distribution (unreleased balls score 0), rack-level correlation rho with a beta-binomial prior from nba.within_game_make_dispersion, point weights from nba.contest_format_rules_ledger; run 20000 simulations of round 1, top-three advancement, final round (score resets) and a shoot-off on ties; output P(win), P(advance). As-of = last field change or rack-placement announcement.
free_sources: Own simulation from public shooting data
nba.threept_contest_score_pmf.why: Directly produces the winner distribution the contest series settles on, including tie mass and field-size effects.

nba.contest_shooting_skill_transfer.label: Transfer of shooter skill to the contest's rack conditions
nba.contest_shooting_skill_transfer.mechanism: Contest make probability is stationary-catch-and-shoot skill from fixed rack spots, with no defender, no movement, rhythm over about a minute and fatigue; it is only partly predicted by game 3P%.
nba.contest_shooting_skill_transfer.rationale: Game 3P% mixes shot difficulty and defence, so contest make rate is better proxied by catch-and-shoot or open-shot 3P%, free-throw skill and past contest make rate, each shrunk because contest samples are 25 balls. Deep-range pull-up shooters can underperform because the contest rewards form repeatability, and a venue's backdrop and rims add a shared level shift.
nba.contest_shooting_skill_transfer.measurement: Per entrant: posterior make rate = precision-weighted mean of (a) catch-and-shoot 3P% on open and wide-open attempts, last 3 seasons, half-life 1 season, shrunk toward league mean with a prior strength k (placeholder 300 attempts, to be fitted by cross-validation on past contests), (b) FT% logit scaled by a fitted slope, (c) past contest make rate shrunk with k (placeholder 75 balls); contest-conditions offset = mean residual of all entrants in the same contest-year (venue-year effect); units = P(make) per ball before location adjustment; as-of = day before.
free_sources: NBA Stats shooting splits by closest defender
Past contest box scores on NBA.com
raw_data: Catch-and-shoot attempts and makes by defender distance
nba.contest_shooting_skill_transfer.why: Different from in-game 3P% because the contest strips out the defender and movement, so the right skill measure for the series is not the default player shooting input.

nba.dunk_judge_score_model.label: Dunk Contest judging panel score and tiebreak model
nba.dunk_judge_score_model.mechanism: The winner is selected by a panel's subjective scores per dunk; round-one two-dunk totals pick the two finalists and the finalists' two final-round dunks alone decide the champion (rules); panel composition, scoring scale and the compression of scores near the maximum decide who wins and whether a dunk-off is needed.
nba.dunk_judge_score_model.rationale: Scores cluster at the top of the scale so many dunks tie, and a run of 10s from celebrity judges can erase a difficulty advantage. Judges anchor on crowd reaction and narrative as well as difficulty, creating a first-mover and last-mover effect, and repeat winners can be penalised or rewarded depending on the panel's era.
nba.dunk_judge_score_model.measurement: From past contests extract every dunk's judge scores; fit an ordinal model of dunk score on (attempt number, make flag, prop use, dunker's reputation, round, panel mean leniency) with a partial-pooling judge effect; estimate per-panel mean and SD and the probability of a perfect score; store panel composition as announced (as-of = announcement); output expected round-one totals, P(advance), final-round two-dunk totals (round one does not carry over) and P(tie) per finalist pair. Use only rounds since the current scale was introduced.
free_sources: NBA.com contest recaps with judge scores
nba.dunk_judge_score_model.why: The series settles on judges' scores, so the process is scoring behaviour and not athletic ability alone.

nba.dunk_difficulty_make_model.label: Dunk difficulty tier and make probability under attempt caps
nba.dunk_difficulty_make_model.mechanism: A contestant's score depends on choosing a dunk of a given difficulty tier and converting it within the attempt allowance; misses burn time or attempts and zero or lower the score.
nba.dunk_difficulty_make_model.rationale: Hard dunks have a high ceiling but a real miss rate, and the attempt cap makes the score a mixture between a clean mid-tier dunk and a failed high-tier one. Props, teammate assists and limited rehearsal affect conversion; contestants who tend to over-script get penalised for misses.
nba.dunk_difficulty_make_model.measurement: Classify each past dunk by difficulty tier (360 or windmill, leap over a person, double-ball, two-step, prop-assisted) from video-coded tags; compute per-dunker attempt success by tier with Beta(2,2) shrinkage, and expected score per dunk = P(make before cap) times mean judged score of the tier plus (1 - P) times the miss score; as-of = last contest participated; units = points per dunk.
nba.dunk_difficulty_make_model.why: Converts a dunker's repertoire into expected judged score under the series' own attempt rules.

nba.dunker_pedigree_profile.label: Dunker athletic profile and prior contest record
nba.dunker_pedigree_profile.mechanism: Contest strength comes from leaping ability, creativity and show experience, none of which appear in regular-season box scores.
nba.dunker_pedigree_profile.rationale: Contest entrants are often bench or G League players whose NBA stats say little, so talent is measured by prior contest finishes, highlight dunk rate, vertical measures from draft combine and age. The sample is tiny and selection is heavy, so pedigree must be shrunk toward a field mean and treated as a ranking, not a number.
nba.dunker_pedigree_profile.measurement: Per announced entrant: pedigree = mean of within-field percentile ranks of (a) contest score = sum over prior contests of points (win 3, final 2, appeared 1) * 0.7^(years since), (b) max vertical z-score from the Draft Combine (missing: field mean plus a missing flag with 0 weight), (c) dunks per 100 minutes over the last two seasons (NBA plus G League), shrunk to the position mean with prior weight 200 minutes; equal weights 1/3 each, plus a G League/non-NBA flag reported separately. Rank within the announced field; as-of = field announcement date.
free_sources: NBA Draft Combine measurements (drafted players only)
Basketball-Reference and G League play-by-play dunk counts
raw_data: In-game dunk counts (NBA and G League)
nba.dunker_pedigree_profile.why: Gives the only pregame talent signal for a contest where season performance is nearly irrelevant.

nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.label: Contest field changes: withdrawal and replacement hazard
nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.mechanism: The entrant list for the 3-point and dunk contests is announced weeks ahead and changes through injury, rest, ASG replacement and sponsor negotiation, which changes both the field strength and the winner's probability.
nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.rationale: A late replacement is usually weaker or different in type, and a withdrawal of the favourite lifts every remaining entrant; the market question requires a specific named player so this is also an eligibility risk.
nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.measurement: Per announced entrant: base withdrawal rate w0 = (withdrawals + 1)/(announced entrants + 8) counted over 3PT/dunk/skills fields 2010-2026 from NBA.com announcements; logistic update with covariates current injury status (Out/Doubtful/Questionable from nba.injuries_pit at the latest vintage), also-in-All-Star-Game flag and also-in-Rising-Stars flag, ridge 1.0. P(participates) = 1 - P(withdraw). P(win | participates) from the contest score model for the actual announced field; replacements drawn from the next-ranked non-entrants by prior contest pedigree. As-of = each daily injury report and announcement time.
free_sources: ESPN and The Athletic reporting archives
raw_data: Announced contest field by date and year
Entrant also in All-Star Game or Rising Stars flag
nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.why: Winner probabilities depend on the final field, so field risk is its own input in these series.

nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile.label: Three-point contest location, deep-ball and release-tempo profile per shooter
nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile.mechanism: Contest score depends on accuracy at each rack location, on deep-range accuracy for the bonus balls between racks, on where the shooter places the all-money-ball rack, and on how many balls he releases before 70 seconds expire.
nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile.rationale: Pooled open 3P% hides location splits: a corner specialist gains by placing the all-money rack in his best corner, and the deep bonus balls reward a 27+ ft make rate that many spot-up shooters lack. The 70-second limit (rules) means slow releasers leave balls unshot, a zero that pooled accuracy never sees.
nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile.measurement: Per shooter: map shotchartdetail 3PA coordinates (LOC_X, LOC_Y) to the five contest racks (corner left/right, wing left/right, top) by distance from the rack position; 3P% by rack over the last 3 seasons shrunk to the shooter's pooled 3P% with k estimated by method of moments (default 150 attempts until estimated), 27+ ft 3P% shrunk to the league deep rate with k estimated (default 100). Tempo = balls released per round and seconds remaining from his past contest rounds (median and sd); if none, impute from the median of previous contestants with a similar release speed from tracking (labelled imputed). Rack placement = announced choice, else the rack maximising expected points. Output P(make) by ball type and balls released; as-of: rack announcement.
free_sources: NBA Stats shot dashboard and shot-location splits
raw_data: shot-level 3PA with x,y location and distance
nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile.why: Converts a shooter into the contest's own scoring geometry and time limit, which the series settles on.

nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.label: Shooting Stars team shooting skill and format conversion
nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.mechanism: A Shooting Stars team (2026: four teams of two NBA players plus one NBA Legend; only Team Knicks of the four team names is franchise-named) scores by making shots from seven locations in order within a 1:10 clock; the team with the higher final-round score wins.
nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.rationale: Kalshi's KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS rules give only the team name and event date (rules_secondary is empty), so the format comes from the official NBA 2026 Kia Shooting Stars rules PDF (read directly 2026-11-09, sha256 ed035e65...b921; completeness/source_provenance/NBA_2026_Shooting_Stars.json): four teams of three (two NBA players plus one NBA Legend); seven locations shot in order 1 to 7 worth 2, 2, 2, 3, 2, 3, 4 points (right-lane layup/dunk, 18-ft right baseline, right elbow, right-wing three, top of the key, left-corner three, long-range three); each player takes one shot at each of locations 1-6 in the team's declared shooting order and at location 7 players shoot in that order as many times as the clock allows; a designated passer at the left wing feeds each shot; the team advances as a unit; 1:10 clock per team per round; the top two of four teams advance from round 1; the lower round-1 team shoots first in the final and the higher final-round score wins; a tied round-1 result that decides advancement is rerun among the tied teams only at 30 seconds (round-1 scores ignored); a tied final is rerun for the full 1:10; a shot out of the declared player order does not count (and, other than at location 7, that player does not shoot again); a team is disqualified if not all players make valid attempts from a location or if it shoots from locations out of order. What stays unknown: how Kalshi applies those rules to settlement and, from the PDF itself, what counts as a valid shot attempt, what disqualification does to a team's score or advancement, whether the 30-second tiebreaker still runs locations 1-6 in full, and whether the two players must be current NBA players. Four of the seven locations (right-lane layup/dunk, 18-ft right baseline, right elbow, top of the key) are 2-point spots, so make rates there come from nba.shooting_stars_two_point_spot_skill and only the right-wing three, left-corner three and long-range three come from nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile. A Legend is likely to have little or no current shooting data, so team skill mixes current rates for active players with older evidence; tempo matters as in the 3PT contest.
nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.measurement: FORMAT (verified from the official NBA rules PDF, sha256 ed035e65...b921): 4 teams x 3 players (2 NBA players + 1 NBA Legend); locations 1-7 in order = right-lane layup/dunk 2, 18-ft right baseline 2, right elbow 2, right-wing three 3, top of the key 2, left-corner three 3, long-range three 4; at locations 1-6 each player takes one shot in the team's declared order, at location 7 players shoot in that order as many times as the clock allows; a left-wing passer feeds each shot; the team advances as a unit; clock = 1:10 per team per round; round 1 = all four teams, top two advance; the lower round-1 team shoots first in the final; the higher final-round score wins (that round-1 scores do not otherwise carry is an inference from this wording, the PDF ignores them explicitly only in the first-round tiebreaker); first-round tiebreaker = tied teams rerun at 30 seconds, only that score counts; final tiebreaker = rerun for the full 1:10; a shot out of the declared player order does not count (and outside location 7 that player does not shoot again); a team is disqualified if not all players make valid attempts from a location or if it shoots from locations out of order. SCORE = 2*(correct-order makes at locations 1, 2, 3, 5) + 3*(makes at locations 4, 6) + 4*(makes at location 7). STILL UNKNOWN (PDF silent; carried as explicit labelled assumptions, never as facts): (U1) what a valid shot attempt is; (U2) what disqualification does to a team's score or advancement; (U3) whether the 30-second tiebreaker still runs locations 1-6 in full or only location 7; (U4) how many location-7 attempts each player completes inside 1:10 and whether the clock can run out before location 7 (EMPIRICAL_QUESTION); (U5) whether other editions use the same rules; (U6) Kalshi's treatment of ties, disqualification, replay and cancellation (u10b). Estimation: NBA players' P(make) at the right-wing three, left-corner three and long-range three from nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile and at the 2-point locations from nba.shooting_stars_two_point_spot_skill; legend component: last five career seasons' 3P% and FT% with an age discount of 1.5 points of 3P% per year since retirement, shrunk to past legends' contest make rate with k = 50 shots, plus a shot-tempo term for the legend's attempts inside the clock; simulate 20,000 contests under the verified rules including the round-1 selection of two of four, with the tiebreak rules and a disqualification and out-of-order branch as labelled assumptions (size of the branch is empirical, not stated by the PDF), and report P(win). CONTRACT CONSTRAINT: KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS settles on which named team wins the contest; the 30-second rerun matters only when a tie decides the second final slot, the full 1:10 rerun only if the final ends level, and Kalshi's text has no tie, shoot-off, disqualification or team-change clause, so a tie is settled by whatever the league declares.

nba.shooting_stars_two_point_spot_skill.label: Shooting Stars two-point-spot skill: layup/dunk, baseline, elbow and top-of-key conversion and release tempo
nba.shooting_stars_two_point_spot_skill.mechanism: Four of the seven Shooting Stars locations (right-lane layup/dunk, 18-ft right baseline, right elbow, top of the key) are 2-point locations (official 2026 rules PDF) whose make rates depend on rim finishing and catch-and-shoot mid-range skill and on how fast the shooter receives the pass and releases; they are not predicted by three-point spot accuracy.
nba.shooting_stars_two_point_spot_skill.rationale: nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile is built from three-point locations and the 27+ ft rate, so with four of seven locations worth two points it leaves most of the circuit without a skill estimate. Layup/dunk locations are near-certain for current athletes, so the differentiator there is time per attempt and, for a legend, whether he can still finish at the rim; baseline, elbow and top-of-key are mid-range catch-and-shoot shots where current players have season data and legends do not. The location list and point values are taken from the official 2026 rules PDF (read directly 2026-11-09, sha256 ed035e65...b921).
nba.shooting_stars_two_point_spot_skill.measurement: Per player and per 2-point location type. Rim location: P(make) from uncontested restricted-area finishing (dunk and layup action types) over the last 3 seasons, shrunk to the position-group rate with k = 60 attempts (placeholder); the main output there is seconds per attempt. Baseline, elbow and top of key: mid-range FG% by zone (left/right baseline, elbow, free-throw-line extended) over 3 seasons from shot-level rows, shrunk to the player's overall mid-range rate with k = 80 attempts (placeholder); a catch-and-shoot restriction by zone is UNVERIFIED and UNAVAILABLE from any free source shown here, so until one is found the rate is an all-attempt mid-range rate flagged as contested-biased, blended with career FT% at weight 0.3 (placeholder) when attempts are below 40. Legends: last five career seasons' mid-range FG% and FT% with an age discount of 2 points of mid-range FG% per year since retirement (placeholder), shrunk to the legend pool with k = 50 shots; rim finishing for a legend is an imputed rate with a flagged ceiling. Tempo: seconds from pass to release per location type (hand-coded). The official 2026 rules PDF fixes the point values (2 at locations 1, 2, 3 and 5), the one-shot-per-player rule at locations 1-6 and the declared shooting order; which player shoots which location is the team's pre-declared order (one shot each at locations 1-6, so each of the three players shoots every 2-point location once). Output per-player P(make) and seconds per attempt for the four 2-point location types; as-of = team and shooting-order announcement.

interactions.mechanism: Win probability is a max-of-noisy-scores function of per-ball make rates, so a shooter's gain from a few points of make probability is bigger when the field is thin at the top and shrinks as more strong shooters enter.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the field with and without the best entrant and compare the change in each remaining entrant's P(win); check against historical favourite hit rates by field strength spread.

interactions.mechanism: Judged score saturates near the scale maximum, so extra difficulty adds little once a clean dunk already earns near-perfect marks, while a miss subtracts a lot; this reverses the naive hard-dunk advantage.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress dunk score on difficulty tier and make flag with a ceiling-aware ordinal model and compare the marginal effect of tier among clean dunks versus the miss penalty.

interactions.mechanism: A withdrawal changes the winner probability differently depending on the number of finalists and rounds: with fewer rounds a replacement has a larger chance to win through variance.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare historical outcomes for replacement entrants against the pre-event field ranking, split by number of rounds.

interactions.mechanism: The gain from placing the all-money rack at a shooter's best location depends on the ball values and whether deep bonus balls exist in that year's format; a large location split is worth more when money balls carry double value and less when deep balls dominate the maximum.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate expected round score with optimal versus average rack placement under each historical format vector and compare with announced placements and realised scores.

interactions.mechanism: With the verified spot values (2, 2, 2, 3, 2, 3, 4), a make at the long-range last spot (location 7) is worth twice a layup and location 7 allows ordered attempts until the clock expires while locations 1-6 give each player one attempt, so a team's expected score depends on the NBA players' and the legend's long-range rate and on how many location-7 attempts remain after the first six locations; a legend with a poor long-range rate is cheap at the layup spot but, because players shoot in declared order at location 7, still costs attempts there, so team skill is a lineup-and-spot assignment, not a team average. Which player takes how many location-7 attempts inside 1:10 is an empirical question.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate team scores under the verified rules with each player's spot make rate and alternative lineups, vary the location-7 attempt count, and compare the spread of P(win) across lineups with the spread from changing team averages; calibrate attempt counts against the recorded 2026 rounds (paused phase: test design only).

interactions.mechanism: The Shooting Stars winner needs a top-two round-1 score and then a higher final score, so the favourite's advantage is compounded over two noisy draws and the final can be won by a team that was only second in round one. The league PDF states the tie regimes: a round-1 tie that decides advancement is rerun at 30 seconds among the tied teams only (round-1 scores ignored) and a tied final is rerun for the full 1:10, so the tiebreaker rewards different skills (a 30-second clock weights the one-shot locations over location 7); how Kalshi settles a tie is not stated, so the tie regime is its own branch.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the two-round format under the PDF rules with each tiebreak as a labelled branch and compare P(win) by round-1 rank with realised round-1-rank-to-champion frequencies once several editions are logged; confirm Kalshi's treatment separately (unknown).

interactions.mechanism: The layup/dunk spot is close to certain for most current athletes, so on that spot the difference between teams is seconds per attempt, while on the baseline, elbow and top-of-key spots a legend's mid-range touch decides whether he costs the team points; the team total therefore depends on tempo at the rim spot and on the legend's mid-range rate, neither of which a three-point profile reveals.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate team scores with per-spot make rates and seconds per attempt from this input, vary the legend's mid-range rate and the rim-spot tempo separately, and compare the spread of P(win) with the spread produced by the three-point spots alone.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in P(win) near the top of the field, flat for low skill
nonlinearities.why: The winner is the maximum of several noisy scores, so top shooters gain disproportionally from higher make rates while low-skill entrants have almost no chance regardless of small skill changes.

nonlinearities.shape: Ceiling at the maximum score with heavy tie mass
nonlinearities.why: Scores are bounded and compressed at the top, so differences in dunk quality translate into almost no score difference above a threshold and the winner is then decided by ties and dunk-offs.
Because withdrawal resolves No, a named entrant's Yes probability is capped by P(participates), which falls sharply with an injury status change rather than linearly.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in P(win) for the top team, with a step in value at the highest-point spot and a possible disqualification branch (consequence not stated in the PDF)
nonlinearities.why: The champion is the maximum of two noisy team scores after an advancement cut, so a modest team-skill edge gives a larger edge in the final than in round one; the last location is worth 4 points against 2 or 3 elsewhere and allows ordered repeat attempts, which makes a long-range specialist more valuable than a flat rate average suggests; an out-of-order shot removes its points and a disqualification (consequence unstated) could cut a score discontinuously, so small differences in make rate or tempo need not map linearly to P(win).
